mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods with declining GDP, or GDP growth and SPX returns show no significant negative correlation (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it indicates a strong labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% each in a month signals a strengthening demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer and investment spending rise.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS increase > 5% each in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS does not significantly correlate with positive SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure in a high-rate environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint condition of high FEDFUNDS and increasing CPIAUCSL does not significantly correlate with negative SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP (GDPC1) coupled with an increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% in a month signals a weakening demand environment exacerbated by labor market stress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decline and UNRATE increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint decline in GDPC1 and increase in UNRATE does not significantly correlate with negative SPX returns (p > 0.05).
